text: Brodie Smith is a former American Ultimate Disc League (AUDL) player and current professional disc golf player and YouTube personality best known for his frisbee trick shot videos. He rose to prominence as a premier ultimate player at the University of Florida, where he won two USA Ultimate College Championships in 2006 and 2010. He also won two National Club Championships: first in 2012 with Austin's Doublewide and again in 2014 with Denver's Johnny Bravo. He has played professionally with the AUDL's Indianapolis AlleyCats, Chicago Wildfire, Dallas Roughnecks, and Jacksonville Cannons. Brodie achieved internet fame in 2011 when his Frisbee Trick Shots video went viral on YouTube. As of July 2018, his channel has over 2 million subscribers and 300 million total video views. Clips of his trick shots have been featured on ESPN's SportsCenter "Top Plays" segment multiple times and on other major media outlets, including the Huffington Post. He has a sponsored line of merchandise produced by DiscStore.com. He appeared in the 28th installment of The Amazing Race alongside Ultimate teammate and friend Kurt Gibson, finishing 5th. As of 2020, he is a professional disc golf player on the DGPT (Disc Golf Pro Tour) and is currently signed to Discraft. Brodie was introduced to Ultimate at Nease High School in Ponte Vedra, Florida, where he began playing in games after cross country practice. He began playing on the University of Florida ultimate team in 2006; that spring, the team won their first National College Championship. In 2007, the UF team finished 3rd, in 2008 they finished as the runner-up, and in 2009 they were eliminated in the Regional Qualifier. In 2010, the UF men's team won their second national championship in five years. Brodie began his professional ultimate career with the AUDL in 2011 playing for the Indianapolis AlleyCats. In 2013, he signed with the Chicago Wildfire, but suffered a knee injury in 2013 that tore his ACL and meniscus, preventing him from playing in 2014 and 2015. In 2016, he signed with the Dallas Roughnecks. In 2017, he returned to Florida and signed with the Jacksonville Cannons. His first trick shot video, Frisbee Trick Shots, was released in 2011 on YouTube as a compilation of trick frisbee throws around Gainesville, Florida, and the University of Florida campus. As of December 2015, the video had generated over 5 million views. In the video, Brodie completes throws into trash cans and other targets in increasingly difficult situations, with the final shot involving him throwing a disc into a trash can from the top of the University of Florida football stadium. Brodie has performed trick shots worldwide, including competing in a Japanese game show, with the goal of promoting awareness for Ultimate as a sport. Some of these videos are uploaded to his Instagram account and to his fan page @brodiesmith21fans. His trick shot videos have also led to multiple appearances on ESPN SportsCenter's Top Plays. Brodie has also created several videos with YouTube trick shot performers Dude Perfect.
